LESSON: WRITING 10.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING: DESCRIPTIVE COMPOSITION (120 -160 WORDS)

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words), part of Strand 10 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How do we describe things or events? 2. Why is it important to describe things or events clearly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a sample composition from print or electronic sources,

2. talk about people or things in the text,

3. make sentences to describe

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a sample composition from print or electronic sources,
2. talk about people or things in the text,
3. make sentences to describe

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration is developed as the learner collaboratively makes sentences to describe how

they spent their leisure time collaboratively.

• Learning to learn is enhanced as the learner builds on reflective learning by creating own compositions and

proofreading the composition written by peers.

Values:
Respect is fostered as the learner writes descriptive compositions about various characters.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills Education is nurtured as the learner acquires effective communication skills when organising and writing

compositions.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can apply descriptive composition writing skills to Kiswahili as they learn the same concept.
